chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding the adhan on the Day of ʿArafah is that one should give the adhan and iqamah for Zuhr, then perform the prayer, then stand and give the iqamah for ʿAsr without an adhan; and likewise for Maghrib and ʿIshaʾ at Muzdalifah.

key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the call announcing the beginning of salat (prayer)
key_terms.اَلسُّنَّةُ: the prescribed prophetic practice in this ruling
key_terms.بِمُزْدَلِفَةَ: at Muzdalifah, the hajj station where Maghrib and ʿIshaʾ are joined
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah during hajj
key_terms.يُقِيمَ: to give the iqamah commencing the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) for the adhan and iqamah on the Day of ʿArafah and at Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This hadith states the sunnah (prophetic tradition) for combining prayers during hajj at ʿArafah and Muzdalifah. It indicates that a single adhan is given for the first prayer, while the second prayer is established with iqamah only.
